correctness.rationale: In the orthonormal shifted Legendre basis the endpoint constants in the antiderivative cancel at x=0, and for n>=m>=1 the only coefficients are a_n at n+1 and -a_(n-1) at n-1. The squared column norm is [1/(2n-1)-1/(2n+3)]/8, giving the full Hilbert–Schmidt identity by telescoping. The window Gram matrix is the compression to m<=n<=floor(Rm). For a fixed power j, only paths with steps 0 and +/-2 closing at n contribute to its trace. The scaled entries on each such path are uniformly those of the frozen coefficients at n/m up to o(1) away from O(j) boundary sites; integrating their Fourier symbol picks the closing paths. This gives the stated bulk symbol, including both parity sectors, with normalization 1/m. The shift norm bound makes continuous functional calculus by polynomial approximation valid on a common spectral interval. For p>1 the removed columns have Schatten norm O((Rm)^(1/p-1)); the triangle inequality for the rescaled norms followed by R to infinity justifies the global moment limit. The angular beta integral gives the gamma constant. For finite m, JP_<m has rank at most m and the classical unfiltered Volterra sequence and index interlacing squeeze the tail to 1/(pi j), proving the membership threshold. For the fixed-k edge, the two shift norms give limsup at most 1/2 and a nonnegative continuous function supported above any positive squared threshold below 1/4 detects linearly many window values there. Min–max transfers that lower bound to the full operator. evidence: Integration by parts identifies the high-moment input restriction isometrically via differentiation with H_0^1 constrained to have moments through degree m-2 zero, norm ||u'||_2; the nonzero singular values are those of its embedding into L2.

Independent stronger equivalence, not claimed in the frozen finding: split the input into the two parities, then gauge the signed shift coefficients. The two blocks are off-diagonal parts of compact symmetric half-line Jacobi matrices with off-diagonal a_n, on indices n>=N for N=m-1 and m, respectively. A block's singular values are the positive eigenvalues of its bipartite Jacobi matrix. At s=1/(2z) the square-summable recurrence solution is proportional to sqrt(2n+1) J_(n+1/2)(z) by the Bessel three-term recurrence and fixed-argument factorial decay; a constant Jacobi Wronskian tending to zero gives uniqueness. The first row leaves residual J_(N-1/2)(z)/(2 sqrt(2N+1)), hence the singular-value multiset is the union of the reciprocals 1/(2j_(m-3/2,k)) and 1/(2j_(m-1/2,k)).

value.rationale: Polynomial orthogonality is a canonical spectral preprocessing choice distinct from best rank-m approximation. The sharp worst-case attenuation and all-real Schatten profile quantify both the extremal and distributed residual integration errors, and the exact square mass provides an all-cutoff normalization. The density plus separate outlier and infinite-tail controls address a substantive family of infinite operators, not a finite numerical table or routine reparameterization of the ordinary Volterra spectrum.
